extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system doing computations with finitely-presented groups (computational group theorists, algebraists, advanced students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational criteria for computing with finitely-presented groups in Magma, including coset enumeration (Todd–Coxeter), coset spaces, subgroup constructions, permutation representations, rewriting/simplifying presentations, low-index subgroup searches, and finite-group order/representation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of zero return from ToddCoxeter/Index/Order
rubrics_metrics.description: A zero value returned by a function invoking the Todd–Coxeter method (or Order/Index that rely on it) indicates the enumeration has failed to complete using the given memory/parameters; no mathematical conclusion (e.g., that index is infinite) can be drawn from this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If zero is returned, try different parameter values (increase CosetLimit, change Hard or Strategy, increase memory) or use more sophisticated techniques; do not assume infinitude from a zero return.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetLimit parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetLimit gives an upper limit on the number of cosets that may be defined at any stage of the coset enumeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default ≈ 1,000,000 divided by number of generators; for large-index or hard enumerations increase CosetLimit; for some tasks you may want to lower it. Hard enumerations often create many more intermediate cosets than the final index, so set CosetLimit accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print parameter (verbosity during enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Print controls the level of informative printing during execution: 0 = no printing, 1 = statistics at termination, 2 = periodic progress messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Print := 2 to observe trends (Max, Total, RD alive, RC alive) and decide whether enumeration is likely to finish; combine with Grain to set reporting frequency. Default is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grain parameter (report frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grain sets the frequency (every m cosets) at which progress messages are printed when Print >= 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default Grain = 10000; set smaller (e.g., 500) to get more frequent updates for hard enumerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard parameter (processing style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard is a boolean indicating expectation of difficulty; when true Magma processes relators in coset-table style rather than relator style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting Hard := true can substantially reduce the maximum number of cosets defined (Max) and improve chances of success for enumerations of large index or hard examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy parameter (fine control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy allows more precise control over the Todd–Coxeter enumeration strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are in the Handbook; change Strategy when default strategy exhausts resources. Combine with CosetLimit, Hard and Print for best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CosetSpace for (in)complete coset tables
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetSpace(G,H) constructs the (complete or incomplete) indexed coset space V of H in G and shares the same parameters as ToddCoxeter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete coset spaces (some cix unknown) can be used to build subgroups properly containing H; complete coset spaces provide permutation representations. You often need to override defaults for hard cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of coset-space completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: IsComplete(V) returns true if the coset space V is complete (every product c_i x known); otherwise V is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete coset spaces are still useful (e.g., to find excluded conjugates), but certain operations (like extracting full permutation representations) require completeness or additional handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting Print output fields (RD alive, Max, Total)
rubrics_metrics.description: RD alive gives number of cosets active at print time, Max is the maximum number of cosets defined simultaneously, Total is cumulative number defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor these values in Print:=2 output to judge whether an enumeration is growing unstably (e.g., Max >> expected index) and to decide parameter adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExcludedConjugates usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ExcludedConjugates(V) (or ExcludedConjugates(T)) returns conjugates of subgroup generators by group generators that lie outside H according to the (complete or incomplete) coset space/table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ExcludedConjugates to find elements to adjoin when attempting to close a set of subgroup generators under conjugation (useful for building derived subgroups or closing under conjugation iteratively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative construction of derived subgroup via coset spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute the derived subgroup G', begin with commutator generators S, build V = CosetSpace(G, sub<G|S>), compute E = ExcludedConjugates(V), set S := S ∪ E and repeat until E is empty; return sub<G|S>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algorithm relies on Todd–Coxeter/CosetSpace and may need adjusted parameters (CosetLimit, Hard) for success. It constructs S closed under conjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup construction operations (functions available)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma provides operations to construct conjugates H^x, intersections H meet K, Core(G,H) (largest normal in H), MaximalOvergroup, MinimalOvergroup, Normalizer(G,H), NormalClosure(G,H), SchreierGenerators, SchreierSystem, Transversal, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations can compute many subgroup relationships and are usable when subgroups are given by generating words or coset tables; use them to obtain subgroup presentations, overgroups, normalizers, transversals, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean subgroup predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean operations exist: H eq K, IsConjugate(G,H,K), u in H, IsNormal(G,H), H subset K, IsMaximal(G,H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to test subgroup relationships; some (e.g., IsConjugate) also provide conjugating elements when true.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetAction and kernel limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetAction(G,H) returns a homomorphism of G into a permutation group and its image when G and H are fp-groups, but the kernel of the action is difficult to compute unless the index of the kernel in G is very small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need the kernel, use CosetKernel(G,H) or Core(G,H). For very large indices CosetAction may fail and you should construct CosetSpace and extract the representation via table operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing large permutation representations
rubrics_metrics.description: For very large index representations CosetAction may fail; instead construct a parameterized CosetSpace(G,H) (with tuned CosetLimit, Fill Factor, CT/RT Factors, Hard) and then extract the permutation image using CosetAction(V), CosetImage(V), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune CosetLimit, Fill Factor, CT Factor, RT Factor and set Hard := true as in the Harada–Norton example. Expect large memory/time; monitor Print output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing subgroups for permutation representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A suitable subgroup (often core-free) is required to obtain a useful permutation representation; sometimes this subgroup is known from the presentation or may be found by sampling random words or using systematic low-index search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unknown, try random-word subgroups or LowIndexSubgroups up to a modest bound; use domain knowledge of the presentation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite(G,H) behavior and Simplify option
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite(G,H) returns an fp-group K isomorphic to H and embedded in G; by default Rewrite performs simplification on the rewritten presentation but will not generally produce the presentation on H's original generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set Simplify := false to turn off automatic simplification if you need original generators or shorter relations; simplified presentations may eliminate many generators but produce long relations which can be harmful for some applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianQuotient and AbelianQuotientInvariants usage
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianQuotient(G,H) abelianizes each relator as it is produced (saving time/memory); AbelianQuotientInvariants(G,H) returns invariant factors and torsion-free rank of H/H'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are useful when attempting to prove G is infinite by finding subgroups with infinite abelian quotient (e.g., an invariant list ending with 0 indicates an infinite summand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify(G) function and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify(G) attempts to eliminate redundant generators and shorten relators by locating substrings matching relation sides; it returns an isomorphic group with a simplified presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter Iterations bounds main elimination loop (default unlimited). One generator often eliminated per iteration. There is also a process-version for interactive control. Controlled simplification may be preferable to aggressive default simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexSubgroups(G,R) behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: LowIndexSubgroups(G,R) returns a sequence of subgroup representatives for conjugacy classes whose index lies in the range described by R (R = integer upper bound or tuple <l,u>); sequence ordered non-decreasing by index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry is a representative for a distinct conjugacy class. Use this to enumerate all subgroups up to a modest index bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexSubgroups parameters: Limit and Subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit (positive integer) causes function to stop after finding n conjugacy classes; Subgroup restricts search to classes where at least one subgroup contains the given subgroup (default trivial subgroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Limit to bound runtime/output. Use Subgroup to focus search on classes containing a particular subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexSubgroups Print levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Print parameter controls intermediate output when LowIndexSubgroups runs: 0 (default) no intermediate printing; 1 prints index, length and generators per class; 2 also prints permutation representation on right cosets; 3 also prints generators for normalizer and right coset representatives for N in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use higher print levels for diagnostic information or when you need the permutation representation/normalizer info during the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexProcess usage and safe iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: LowIndexProcess(G,R) creates an interactive process that returns control after each class is found; use ExtractGroup(P), ExtractGenerators(P) to inspect current class and NextSubgroup(~P) to advance. Use IsEmpty(P) to check for completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NextSubgroup requires the tilde (~) because it modifies P. If you call ExtractGroup on an empty process you'll get a runtime error; test IsEmpty(P) before extracting to avoid errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order(G) strategy and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Order(G) tries to deduce |G| by reducing to coset enumeration over the trivial subgroup; returns zero if unable. Order takes the same parameters as Index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default memory allocation for coset enumeration is small; increase CosetLimit for larger/difficult finite groups or adopt more sophisticated methods such as constructing a chain of subgroups G ≥ H1 ≥ ... ≥ Hr = {1} showing each finite index, or locate known subgroups of known order from the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proving infinitude via subgroups or homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: To show G is infinite, either find a subgroup with an infinite abelian quotient (detected via AbelianQuotientInvariants returning a 0 entry) or construct a surjective homomorphism onto a known infinite group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques are artful in practice; subgroup-rewriting and abelian-quotient computations can help detect infinite sections. The Rewrite + AbelianQuotientInvariants/AbelianQuotient workflow is highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing representations for known finite-structure classes
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is a p-group use the p-quotient algorithm to produce a pc-group K; if G is soluble use the soluble quotient algorithm; otherwise construct a permutation representation over a core-free subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose algorithm appropriate to group structure. For very large finite groups expect heavy computation; permutation representations often require finding a core-free subgroup of manageable index. Magma plans future support for Cayley-graph multiplication table representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abelian group constructors and element representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct free/finitely-presented abelian groups with FreeAbelianGroup(n), AbelianGroup<...|...>, or quo/Fourier-style quo constructors; elements are represented additively and printed in canonical integer-sequence form. ElementToSequence/Eltseq return coordinate vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abelian group elements have canonical printed forms and equality testing works (unlike general fp-groups). Use the quo constructor to form quotients of non-free abelian groups. Be aware of generator print names vs internal names (printed relations may use $.i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations() and Generators() behavior for abelian quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations() returns the relation list of an abelian group (printed with $.i references to free abelian parent); Generators() prints the current generator images (possibly expressed in other symbols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect Relations output to reference free-parent generator notation ($.i). Generators may print as linear combinations of named generators rather than simple generator symbols.
